pr_title: Add support for the DECSWT (Set Window Title) escape sequence
pr_body:
This PR adds support for the `OSC 21` sequence used on DEC terminals to
set the window title. It's just an alias of the `OSC 2` title sequence
used by XTerm.

This PR also corrects the handling of blank title sequences, which are
supposed to reset the title to its default value, but were previously
ignored.

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

To handle the blank title parsing correctly, I had to make some changes
to the state machine. Previously it would not have dispatched an `OSC`
sequence unless it received a semicolon following the `OSC` number, but
when there's a blank string, that semicolon should not be required.

I also took this opportunity to simplify the `OSC` parsing in the state
machine, and eliminate the `_GetOscTitle` method which no longer served
any purpose.

## Validation Steps Performed

I've manually confirmed that the title sequences are now working as
expected, and added some state machine unit tests covering the blank
value handling for these sequences.

I also had to update one of the existing state machine tests to account
for the changes I made to allow the semicolon to be omitted.

Closes #16783
Closes #16784

issue_context.title: OSC 2 doesn't handle a blank title correctly
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version

1.20.10572.0

### Windows build number

10.0.19045.4046

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

In a WSL bash shell execute, the following statement:
```
printf '\e]2;ERASE THIS\e\\\e]2;\e\\' ; read
```

This is setting the title to "ERASE THIS" and then immediately after setting it to a blank string. The `read` is just to allow time to view the result, in case the shell tries to change the title to something else.

### Expected Behavior

The title should be reset to the default value, or at least a blank title. For example, this is what it looks like in XTerm:
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/assets/4181424/33df2670-3f5e-4d6b-9632-7858d98da92b)


### Actual Behavior

The blank title sequence has no effect, and the title is left as "ERASE THIS":
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/assets/4181424/5f8e5132-8e76-4770-9bc8-248ecd58ee0a)

Note that you should also be able to reset the title with `\e]2\e\\` (i.e. no semicolon after the `2`), although not all terminals support that.

review_comments: All that `_GetOscTitle` was doing was assigning the `wstring_view` to a `wstring`, and checking that it wasn't blank. But we don't actually want that blank check, and there's no reason why we can't just pass the `wstring_view` through to `SetWindowTitle` as is.

I'm not sure why the title parameter originally expected to be null-terminated, but that's no longer the case. The [`CONSOLE_INFORMATION::SetTitle`](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/ad51b22f440a57ff8381499c84e19b9f1d174cab/src/host/consoleInformation.cpp#L217) method immediately constructs a `std::wstring` with that parameter, and in the [`Terminal::SetWindowTitle`](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/ad51b22f440a57ff8381499c84e19b9f1d174cab/src/cascadia/TerminalCore/TerminalApi.cpp#L83) implementation, it's assigned to a `std::optional<std::wstring>` using `emplace`. Neither of those should need a null-terminated `string_view` as far as I understand.
Ah, probably vestiges of the pre-wstring times :)

I dropped the `wch` parameter from this method because it's never actually used for anything. It just indicated whether the sequence was terminated with a `BEL` or an `ST` backslash, but that's of no relevance to anyone.
